| `structural-equality-is-reflexive-bitwise-float` | Choosing the equality/hash semantics for a float (`f32`/`f64`) leaf inside a STRUCTURAL context — a record/enum/tuple field, a `Vec` element, a `HashMap`/`HashSet` key/element — OR deciding whether floats satisfy the `Eq`/`Hash` markers. Also fires when an eligibility gate rejects a leaf "because NaN != NaN". | Structural equality MUST be REFLEXIVE (`x == x` for every `x`, including `NaN`), because it drives dedup, `contains`, and HashMap/HashSet key identity — `x == x → false` is a correctness hole (a value cannot find itself). Reflexivity FORCES bitwise/total float semantics: the eq thunk bit-casts each float to a same-width integer (`f32→i32`, `f64→i64`) and integer-compares the bit patterns (so `NaN == NaN` when the bits match, `+0.0 != -0.0`), NEVER IEEE `fcmp oeq` (which is non-reflexive). The hash thunk MUST hash the SAME bit pattern (bitcast + zext + the shared integer mix) so `==` IMPLIES an equal hash — the eq basis and the hash basis are ONE decision; a mismatch (bitwise eq + numeric hash, or vice versa) silently breaks every map lookup. This is DISTINCT from scalar numeric `==` (a bare `f64 == f64` expression), which stays IEEE (`NaN != NaN`, `+0.0 == -0.0`) and lowers through MIR `FloatCmp`, not the thunk — keep the two paths separate. Floats therefore DO satisfy `Eq` + `Hash` (bitwise/total) but NOT `Ord` (ordering stays IEEE-partial; a total bitwise order is a separate decision). The eligibility gate, the eq thunk, and the hash thunk are THREE consumers of the same verdict and must all agree: a checker that admits a float-bearing aggregate while the thunk fails closed is the cliff this fixes; prove the full chain with a COMPILED `.hew` exec asserting `NaN==NaN` (same bits) is TRUE, `+0.0 == -0.0` is FALSE, and a float-bearing-key HashMap round-trips (insert+get) — value-asserting, not `.len()`. | feat/v06-f64-bitwise-equality (2026-06-27): removed the checker float-eq BLOCK (`eq_eligibility`/`hash_eligibility` `IneligibleFloat` verdict deleted), flipped the `Eq`/`Hash` markers on for floats (Ord stays partial), replaced the `eq_thunk`/`hash_thunk` float fail-closed (`hew-codegen-rs/src/thunks.rs`) with the bitwise compare + bit-pattern hash via `float_bits_int_type`. The same change uniformly enables `Vec<float-record>::contains`, `HashSet<f64>`, bare `HashMap<f64,V>`, and a generic `fn same<T>(a:T,b:T)->bool { a==b }` over a float-bearing T (former eq-thunk bypass) — all route through the one bitwise thunk. Proof gate: a compiled `.hew` exec asserting `NaN==NaN` (identical bits) is true and `+0.0 == -0.0` is false, plus a float-bearing-record-key HashMap insert+get round-trip. |

### `exhaustive-coverage` — no wildcard fallthrough in dispatch or lowering

- **area**: analysis, codegen, match
- **invariant**: Visitors, dispatch chains, and match lowerings must enumerate every supported variant and every operation×type pair. Wildcard or default branches in semantic positions hide gaps as silent wrong code; cross-enum fallback and guarded wildcards count as gaps.
- **why**: Adding a new AST variant or operand type without an exhaustive matrix lets the new shape silently take the default arm. The compiler keeps producing output, but the output is wrong for the new case.

| id | trigger | apply | evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `exhaustive-traversal-and-lowering` | A new AST variant, lowering branch, or supported type is added — **including a new variant on a self-recursive type enum** (e.g. `Ty`) handled by structural walkers. Also fires when a MIR `lower_value` match has a wildcard `_ => None` catch-all that silently swallows an identifiable-but-unimplemented case. | Maintain explicit variant/type lists, build an operation × type matrix for typed lowerings, cover narrow widths and uncommon shapes, and prefer errors over warnings when a case is unsupported. **For a new variant on a recursive `Ty`-shaped enum, audit every self-recursive walker** (`map_children`, `any_child`/`contains_var`, `substitute`/`substitute_named_param` and peers): a pre-existing `_` arm silently treats the new variant as a *leaf*, so `substitute` stops rewriting through it and `contains_var` returns `false` — letting an unresolved `Ty::Var` inside the new variant **escape inference into codegen** (type-inference-boundary breach). This failure is **invisible to a diff-grep** because the offending `_` arms are pre-existing (not `+` lines); only exhaustive matches (no `_`) or cross-ecosystem review catch it. Prefer deleting the `_` wildcard in structural `Ty` walkers so the compiler forces every future variant to be handled. **For `lower_value` wildcard arms:** a `HirExprKind::BindingRef { .. } => None` catch-all is a fail-OPEN class. A `BindingRef { resolved: Item(_), ty: Function }` case falls through silently — `lower_value` returns `None`, the argument is missing, the call emits no output and exits 0. Every MIR `lower_value` catch-all arm must either (a) emit a `NotYetImplemented` diagnostic before returning `None`, or (b) have an explicit comment naming exactly what cases it still covers. **When the new variant is a single-operand borrowing read** (carries one sub-expr the walker just recurses into, e.g. a codec/intrinsic node), the exhaustiveness pass forces an arm at every walker but then `clippy::match_same_arms` (pre-push gate) REJECTS a standalone arm whose body duplicates a sibling — merge it into the existing `Unary { operand, .. }` (or other identical-body) arm via an or-pattern rather than adding a separate arm; expect this at ~8-10 walkers per IR layer (HIR `node.rs` exhaustive matches + MIR `Instr` def/use/source/alias classifiers). | PR #798/#786/#797; `e1fe0c37` (added `Ty::Borrow`; `map_children`/`any_child`/`substitute_named_param` swallowed it via pre-existing `_` until each got an explicit pointee-recursing arm + 3 unit tests proving `contains_var(&Var)`/`&T→&string`/`&Vec<$v>→&Vec<i32>`; caught by cross-eco GPT-5.5 review, not by the diff). `feat/named-fn-as-value` (lower.rs:5496 `BindingRef { .. } => None` swallowed `ResolvedRef::Item(_)` + `Function` type — named fns as values produced silent exit 0, no output; fixed by adding an explicit arm before the wildcard and annotating the wildcard with a comment naming surviving cases). |
| `match-fail-closed` | Match checking or lowering changes. | Forbid cross-enum fallback, treat guarded wildcards as non-exhaustive, exclude `Never` and `Error` from result inference, wrap `HashMap.get()` at the expression boundary, trap on runtime fallthrough, and emit `MirStatement::Bind` (not just `Instr::Move`) at the entry of every arm body that introduces a payload binding — the move-checker dataflow keys on `Bind` to lift the binding from `Uninit` to `Live`, so a bare `Move` into the binding's local trips `InitialisedBeforeUse` on the first arm-body read. **The runtime-fallthrough trap must be UNREACHABLE for any match the checker accepted as exhaustive — a reachable trap on valid input is a silent-wrong miscompile (`check`-green, `run`-exit-1, no output).** When a lowering collapses several arms into a single representative (e.g. "the first `Binding`/`Wildcard` arm is the catch-all"), it silently drops every later arm — including the real `_` default — and the dropped-default path then hits the trap. A `Binding`/`Wildcard` arm is a catch-all ONLY when it has no guard; a guarded binding arm (`x if p => …`) must fall through to the next arm on guard failure. Lower literal/binding/wildcard arms as ONE ordered chain in source order (mismatch OR guard-failure → next arm; final fall-through → trap), never as `leading_literals + Option<single_catch_all>`. Exec-validate (`hew run`, assert stdout) the fall-through path: a `check`-only or MIR-shape test cannot catch a dropped default arm. | Original match correctness audit; `feat/mono-mixed-enum-payload-ctor`; `fix/match-default-arm` (2026-06-02): `lower_match_literal` collapsed all non-literal arms into one `wildcard_arm`, dropping every arm after the first guarded `Binding` (incl. the real `_`); fall-through emitted `Trap{ExhaustivenessFallthrough}` so `match n { 0 => …, x if x>100 => …, _ => … }` on `n=5` exited 1 with no output. Fixed by lowering all arms as one ordered chain; pinned by `match_literal_guard_default_exec.rs`. |

### `lifecycle-symmetry` — every setup has a matched teardown on every exit path

- **area**: control flow, codegen RAII, FFI handles, runtime shutdown, concurrent test cleanup
- **invariant**: Allocations, opened handles, locks, mailboxes, profiler state, and partial select/join setups must be released on every exit path — return, panic, timeout, cancel, shutdown — with exactly one canonical release path per owned thing. Manual `close()` / `free()` and automatic drop must agree on who is canonical.
- **why**: Cleanup paths that only handle the happy case leak under failure; double-cleanup paths free twice. Both are silently catastrophic — the first as accumulating debt, the second as memory corruption.

| id | trigger | apply | evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cleanup-all-exits` | Code stages setup work or mutates side-channel state before success is guaranteed, OR a checker/elaborator is built against a scaffold whose CFG is structurally flat (single basic block) and will widen later. | Evaluate return expressions before drops, reset pending state on failure, deactivate all intermediate loops, and clean partial select/join/ask setup before panicking, timing out, or returning early. When bounded teardown cannot wait for a live worker, transfer ownership to a reaper that performs the final join and free path; treat an outstanding join handle as the worker-liveness authority even if task state already says `Done`. **Teardown that races an in-flight reply must DRAIN the reply send before the close/free barrier, not after.** A graceful `node_stop` that zeroes its `CURRENT_NODE` use-after-free barrier (or sets a "stopping" flag the reply path bails on) BEFORE draining in-flight inbound-ask workers abandons replies those workers already computed: the worker reaches `send_reply_envelope`, sees the barrier tripped, drops the reply, and the peer's reader observes the connection close mid-ask → a spurious `ConnectionDropped` even though the node is still ALIVE and the reply existed. The fix is ordering, not a new lock: close the SPAWN gate (a flag distinct from the UAF/teardown guard so it does not also make in-flight sends bail), drain the per-manager worker counter to zero so earned replies flush while the transport is still up, and only THEN trip the close barrier and free. The drain ceiling must remain (a straggler past it bails fail-closed at the still-present UAF guard), and the spawn gate must be a SEPARATE flag from the reply-bail flag — collapsing them re-introduces the abandon. For runtime-level reset: register every subsystem's cleanup in a session hook registry at init so it fires from every shutdown path. **Resolved gap**: when a Ready/Suspended task is cancelled via `mark_done(Cancelled)`, user-code Drop previously never fired; resources held in those stack frames leaked until process exit. Fixed by adding `HewTask::cancel_cleanup_fn: Option<unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void)>` — a compiler-registered callback invoked (with `env_ptr` as the borrowed argument) before `mark_done(Cancelled)` in both `hew_task_scope_cancel` and `hew_task_scope_cancel_one`. The field is taken (cleared) before the call for idempotence under double-cancel; `env_ptr` deallocation via `hew_rc_drop` in `hew_task_free` is unchanged. Compiler codegen must emit this function to call `@resource close()` and `@linear consume()` for task-captured resources. Regression tests: `scope_cancel_fires_cancel_cleanup_fn_for_ready_and_suspended_tasks`, `cancel_one_fires_cancel_cleanup_fn_for_ready_task`, `cancel_cleanup_fn_fires_at_most_once_on_double_cancel`. For IR-level move-checkers and drop elaborators: a forward-scan that walks a flat `MirStatement` stream is degenerate-correct only under a single-block CFG; the moment `if`/`match`/loop lowering produces real basic blocks, the checker must run as a per-block dataflow over a path-sensitive lattice (in v0.5 the four-state `Uninit \| Live \| Consumed \| MaybeConsumed` lattice on `BindingId`) and drop plans must be enumerated per `Terminator::Return` block — not function-wide. `MaybeConsumed` at any Return exit on a `@linear` binding is a hard `MustConsume` rejection, not a "drop on some paths" recovery. Pin both the lattice meet rules (commutativity + associativity + idempotence) and the per-Return-block drop narrowing as property tests before the CFG-aware lowering merges, so the scaffold-correct-under-flat-MIR substrate cannot regress silently. | PR #801/#794/#1271 (hew_sched_shutdown reset gaps); task-scope cancelled-worker reclamation; fix/fix-task-scope-cleanup-cancel (`HewTask::cancel_cleanup_fn`, taken-before-call for double-cancel idempotence); `hew-mir/src/dataflow.rs` — four-state `Uninit\|Live\|Consumed\|MaybeConsumed` lattice + per-block worklist + per-Return-block drop narrowing replaced the pre-CFG flat-stream scan. fix/v060-connection-lifecycle: `hew_node_stop` drained in-flight inbound-ask reply sends only AFTER zeroing its `CURRENT_NODE` barrier + `mark_stopping`, so a worker that reached `send_reply_envelope` after the barrier dropped its computed reply → spurious `ConnectionDropped` (the two-process remote-ask tests flaked ~5-15% under load, T-01/T-02). Reordered to a Phase-1 drain behind a NEW `HewConnMgr.inbound_spawn_closed` spawn gate (distinct from `reconnect_shutdown`) before the barrier; proven 100/100 under concurrent load on a 32-core host with `--retries 0`, retiring the test-side retry shim. |
| `cyclic-cfg-worklist-rpo` | A dataflow worklist pass is added or changed on a CFG that now contains back-edges (loop lowering, or any new `Terminator::Goto` that targets a lower-ID block). | Seed the worklist in Reverse Post-Order (RPO), not block-ID order. Use a visited-only meet: skip predecessors whose exit-state has not yet been computed when computing the entry state of the current block. Run diagnostics in a separate sweep after the fixpoint converges, using the stable exit states from the fixpoint pass — never emit diagnostics inside the fixpoint loop itself. ID-order iteration on cyclic CFGs processes a block's successor (body_bb) before some of that block's predecessors (overhead blocks allocated by checked-arithmetic such as overflow_trap_bb have IDs higher than body_bb), so the body block's entry state is computed with stale or absent predecessor states, injecting false Uninit contributions that survive in the dedup set and surface as false-positive `InitialisedBeforeUse` diagnostics. RPO guarantees that on the first sweep every forward-edge predecessor is processed before the block it feeds; true back-edges are the only unvisited predecessors on first pass and are correctly handled by the visited-only filter. | feat/for-while-lowering commits 0b03e2c9 (HIR) and f5206a01 (MIR+dataflow); `hew-mir/src/dataflow.rs:350` (`compute_rpo`), `:230` (`meet_predecessors` visited-only filter), `:652` (`analyze` two-pass fixpoint + diagnostic sweep). |
| `death-signal-fires-on-every-terminal-cause` | Building or extending a terminal-signal delivery path — actor DOWN/EXIT, monitor/link notification, supervisor death callback, cross-node MonitorLost — that must fire when a watched thing reaches a terminal state. Fires especially when the same logical signal is reachable through MORE THAN ONE finalize path (a crash trap vs a clean self-stop finalize vs a connection-drop/partition fan-out). | A death-signal is fail-OPEN until it is proven to fire on EVERY distinct terminal cause, because the causes usually flow through SEPARATE finalize code paths and fixing one leaves the others silent. Enumerate the terminal causes for the watched thing (clean exit, crash, unreachable/partition at minimum) and confirm each routes through a site that emits the signal — do NOT assume one finalize path (e.g. the crash trap `notify_monitors_on_death`) covers a sibling (e.g. the scheduler's `Stopping → Stopped` self-stop finalize, which historically notified the actor-group condvars but NOT monitors). | `container-ingress-ownership-is-per-container` | Migrating a container's element ownership to refcounted/header-aware values, or deciding a container's ingress (`push`/`insert`) and the codegen consume-handling for heap-owning elements. A container fed only already-owned header-aware values (e.g. codegen passing header-aware Hew strings) uses MOVE: store the pointer, and codegen **must** null-after-move the source so exactly one owner remains. A container with headerless/borrowed/throwaway producers (e.g. `hew_string_split`/`lines`) uses COPY-IN: allocate a fresh owned copy, do **not** free the source, and codegen **must not** null-after-move (the source stays caller-droppable). Mismatching is catastrophic and silent: COPY-IN + null-after-move **orphans/leaks** the moved source; MOVE + no-null **double-frees**. This means the blanket "`Vec::push` ⇒ `nullOutDropSlot`" rule in `raii-null-after-move` is *container-specific* — the drop elaborator must derive consume semantics per container ingress contract, including *conditional* consume (map `insert` consumes the key on a vacant slot but the caller retains its duplicate on overwrite). Document the MOVE-vs-copy-in contract and any conditional-consume at the ingress sites so the drop/move-checker derives it correctly. Add non-vacuous refcount-ladder tests asserting MOVE does *not* bump rc while clone does. For COPY-IN specifically, retaining the source is **not** automatic once function-scope drop elaboration runs: a fail-closed drop-derivation *escape scan* that treats a `push`/`set` element operand as an ownership escape will exclude the retained source from the drop-allow set and silently leak it one-inner-collection-per-iteration in a reused/loop-carried accumulator (the source is byte-distinct from the deep clone the container now owns). Exempt the copy-in element stores (`hew_vec_push_owned`/`hew_vec_set_owned`) from that scan so the source keeps its own scope-exit drop — the clone the container holds is an independent allocation freed by `hew_vec_free_owned`, so the source dropping once is correct, not a double-free. Prove it with a low-vs-high **leak-slope oracle** on a loop-carried accumulator, using **literal strings only** (historically f-string interpolation in a loop leaked ~1 alloc per interpolated value and contaminated the measurement — fixed in v0.6 by recognising the `to_string_<ty>` catalog producers in `is_fresh_owned_string_producer`; literal strings remain the safest oracle input regardless). | W5.011-P2b: vec (`cabffcd3`) chose COPY-IN (it has headerless producers like `hew_string_split`); maps (`e210ecbd`) chose MOVE (codegen feeds already-header-aware strings, ZERO headerless producers — copy-in would orphan the source). Discovery initially recommended copy-in "on the same grounds as vec"; the planner corrected it on producer-set evidence. Resolved for nested-collection Vec elements (#1722, `fix/nested-vec-push-ownership`): `Vec<Vec<…>>`/`Vec<HashMap>`/`Vec<HashSet>` route through the owned-descriptor copy-in ABI and the local-collection drop-derivation escape scan now exempts `hew_vec_push_owned`/`hew_vec_set_owned`, so the retained source drops exactly once — pinned by `hew-cli/tests/nested_vec_push_leak_oracle.rs` (leak slope) + `tests/hew/nested_vec_push_test.hew` (copy-in contents). The plan had assumed copy-in would *automatically* stop the alias-group pass from suppressing the source free; it did not — the escape scan needed the explicit exemption. #2033 (`fix/v06-vec-iter-hashmap-overwrite-leaks`): the conditional-consume the rule names is now MATERIALISED in codegen — `HashMap/HashSet.insert` return an `i1` (vacant=true / overwrite=false); the move-checker still statically consumes the key (suppressing its scope-exit drop) and codegen branches on that `i1` to release the caller's duplicate key ONLY on the overwrite path (`hew_string_drop` for string keys, `__hew_record_drop_inplace_<R>` for string-bearing record keys) — freed exactly once (vacant by the map, overwrite by the codegen release), pinned by `hashmap_overwrite_key_leak_oracle.rs` (slope + vacant/overwrite scribble exactly-once). #1949 (same lane): the `for x in vec` cursor and its source vec are a SECOND escape-scan-vs-source-free seam — `hew_vec_get_str`/`hew_vec_get_owned` RETAIN the element into the loop var, which the body can MOVE into another owner (`for w in words { map.insert(w,…) }`); freeing the source `Vec<string>`/owned-element vec then runs the per-element release over a value the downstream owner also frees (double-free, caught only under MallocScribble — `leaks` reports 0). The boundary is element-class: the for-in source/cursor vec drop is admitted ONLY for `BitCopy`-element vecs (no retain-and-consume hazard); owned/string-element for-in source vecs stay undropped (leak, fail-closed) pending element-escape accounting. Pinned by `for_in_vec_iter_leak_oracle.rs` (BitCopy slope + owned-element-consumed-into-map scribble no-double-free). LESSON: ANY new "free this collection at scope exit" authority must ask whether its elements are extracted-and-consumed elsewhere, not just whether the handle escapes. |

| `leak-on-insert-not-before-dedup` | A "register once per key" side table interns/`Box::leak`s a fresh `&'static` value, OR commits any other irreversible side-effect (leak, global insert, fd dup, counter bump), and the dedup/first-wins decision is keyed downstream of where the irreversible step runs — especially when the registrant fires once-per-*use* (per spawn / per call) but the table dedups once-per-*type*/key. | Do the irreversible step **only on the committing branch**, under the same lock/decision that dedups — pass the value by-move and `Box::leak`/insert inside the `or_insert_with`/vacant arm so a losing or repeat caller drops (frees) its copy instead of orphaning it. | `deferred-reply-channel-single-reaper-typed-drop` | A deferred-delivery channel (ask reply slot, duplex/stream reply) byte-copies a delivered owned payload (String/Bytes/Vec/HashMap/HashSet/Closure, or a record/enum/tuple with an owned leaf) into a buffer the waiter consumes LATER, so the producer's copy and the channel's copy alias one allocation — AND the consume leg can be skipped (await-deadline/timeout, select-loser, explicit cancel, actor-shutdown, or alloc-failure before delivery). | The channel must own a registered typed destructor (a `reply_drop_fn` fn-pointer slot, symmetric to the eventual consume-side drop) and run it as the **single canonical reaper** on EVERY non-consume teardown leg — never-consumed, cancelled-before-delivery, AND alloc-failure — gated on the not-yet-consumed sentinel: consume nulls `value`, so the dtor fires iff `value != null` at final free (consume XOR teardown drops, never both; double-cancel is idempotent because `value` is already null). Codegen is the only place that knows the reply type `R` at each ask site, so it MUST register the dtor fail-closed right after channel construction, before any reply can deposit: bit-copy/user-handle `R` → null (buffer-only free, the prior behaviour), composite `R` → the already-seeded in-place drop thunk, leaf-owned `R` → a synthesised `{ R }`-wrapper drop reusing the canonical aggregate-drop emitter; an owned `R` the classifier cannot map is a hard `CodegenError`, **never a silent null** (a silent null reinstates the exact leak). The producer-side dispatch trampoline must IGNORE the deliver-call's false (not-delivered) return and must NOT free the payload itself — the channel's dtor run is the only drop, else double-free. Keep the field struct-local — do not fold it into a runtime-handle/reply-table refactor. | fix/reply-channel-ownership (#1739/#1735): `hew_reply` byte-copied a delivered owned reply (aliasing embedded heap) and the never-consumed/cancel/OOM legs `libc::free`'d the buffer with NO typed destructor → embedded String/Vec/HashMap/Closure heap leaked on timeout/cancel/select-loser/shutdown; the declared-actor trampoline also ignored `hew_reply`'s false return, so a naive producer-side free would double-free. | `terminal-transition-before-side-effect-that-spawns-a-racing-terminator` | A teardown path (actor trap/stop, handle close) performs an observable side-effect that can make ANOTHER thread independently drive the same object to a terminal state, and only THEN takes its own terminal-state CAS — with a guard that bails out when the object is already terminal. The canonical smell: `close_mailbox(); loop { if already_terminal { return; } CAS(cur → terminal) }`. The side-effect (closing the mailbox) is itself the trigger for the racing terminator (a worker's "mailbox closed while draining → self-STOP" settle), so the order is a lost-notification race, not a benign reordering. | Take the terminal-state CAS that establishes THIS path as the terminating authority FIRST, before the side-effect that can spawn a competing terminator. Once the object is in this path's terminal state, the racing thread's own `Running → Idle` / `Idle → Stopped` settle CAS fails, so it cannot terminate the object out from under you and steal the notification/teardown work this path owes (supervisor child-crashed notify, link/monitor exit propagation). Run the side-effect immediately after the CAS — it is still correct (new sends are already rejected by the terminal state). The bug is SILENT and order-dependent: when the racing self-stop wins, it reaches a DIFFERENT terminal state via a path that does NOT do this path's notification, the original path reads "already terminal" and bails, and the omission surfaces far downstream as a waiter (supervisor `hew_supervisor_wait_restart`) blocking to its full timeout ceiling — never as a local error. Diagnose by instrumenting whether the notification call ran at all (an EMPTY trace between the waiter's ENTER and its CEILING means the notify never fired, i.e. the teardown bailed at the terminal check), not by assuming the wait/notify condvar lost the wake. Reproduces only under load/coverage that widens the window between the side-effect and the CAS; the fix is validated by the harshest-condition pass (N×100 under load + `cargo llvm-cov` with `--retries 0`), and the matching `retries=N` SHIM is deleted in the same change. | fix/v060-supervisor-restart-wake (#58/#2): `hew_actor_trap` closed the child actor's mailbox BEFORE its terminal CAS; a worker mid-dispatch hit the scheduler `activate_actor` "mailbox closed while draining → IDLE → STOPPED" self-stop, won the terminal CAS ~2.5-8% under `cargo llvm-cov` + load, and the trap then read STOPPED and bailed — dropping `hew_supervisor_notify_child_event`, so the nested supervisor's `wait_restart` reached its 30s ceiling. Fixed by moving the terminal CAS before `mailbox_close` in `hew-runtime/src/actor.rs` (`hew_actor_trap`); proven 200/200 under load + llvm-cov where the unfixed binary failed 5/200, then the `child_supervisor_recovery_recreates_nested_subtree` `retries=1` SHIM removed from `.config/nextest.toml`. Cousin of `monotonic-epoch-single-clock` (both are determinism defects exposed by coverage-instrumented contention); the circuit-breaker single-clock fix (`dda7ea08`) was a sibling symptom on the same test family. |
| `terminal-state-is-not-quiescence-when-published-cross-thread` | A free/reclaim path decides an object is safe to free by classifying its lifecycle STATE (`Crashed`/`Stopped`/`Closed`) as quiescent, AND a DIFFERENT thread can publish that terminal state out from under the thread that owns the object's active critical section (e.g. an external `hew_actor_trap` CAS-ing a still-dispatching actor `Running → Crashed`, erasing the `Running` ownership marker the free path relied on). The owner is still reading the object box / arena / mailbox in its post-operation settle when the free reclaims it. Smell: a quiescence predicate that is a pure function of an atomic LIFECYCLE state (`is_quiescent(state) == state ∈ {terminal…}`), with a terminal CAS reachable from a thread other than the active owner. Symptom is a use-after-free that surfaces FAR from the free — a corrupted/reused node read tripping an unrelated fail-closed guard (here the envelope-mode P5.2 dispatch guard aborting 0xc0000005 on a copy-mode-only test), never a clean "freed twice" at the free site. | The terminal lifecycle state alone is NOT proof of quiescence: it proves no NEW work will start, not that the CURRENT owner has finished touching the object. Gate the free on an explicit OWNERSHIP/critical-section marker in addition to the terminal state — a flag the owner sets BEFORE the publishing CAS that makes the object trap-stealable (i.e. before, not after, the `Runnable → Running` CAS) and clears (Release) on EVERY exit of its critical section via an RAII guard, which the free path waits on (Acquire, spin-until-clear with a bounded deadline → fail-closed: leak/`-2` rather than UAF). Setting the flag AFTER the winning CAS is itself a residual instance of the SAME bug: the object is already in the racing state (`Running`) and another thread's terminal CAS can land in the CAS→marker gap, so the free observes terminal-without-marker and reclaims under the owner. Claim before the CAS so the flag is published the instant the object can be observed in the racing state; on a LOST CAS the owner never owned the object, so it must clear the optimistically-set flag on the early-return path (EVERY failure path clears — otherwise a non-owner leaves the flag set and wedges the free to its deadline). The clear-on-lost-CAS cannot clobber a concurrent winner ONLY because the object is single-owner per epoch (single enqueue per `Runnable` transition + single-consumer deque pop); verify that invariant before using a plain bool, else the loser's clear erases the winner's claim and reopens the gap. The Acquire/Release pair makes observing the cleared flag also publish every write the owner made. This mirrors the existing `terminate_finished` wait. Do NOT try to fix it by having the cross-thread terminator drain/clean the object's queue: the queue consumer is single-consumer (`hew_mailbox_try_recv`), so a cross-thread drain is a second concurrent consumer → corruption, and it does not cover the node already in the owner's hand. Verify the RAII guard is the LAST local dropped (so it clears after all object accesses) AND is claimed BEFORE the publishing CAS (not after the CAS win); verify EVERY CAS-failure path clears the optimistically-set flag; verify a terminal object cannot RE-arm the flag (the activation entry's top-of-fn terminal skip must return before the claim). Distinct from `terminal-transition-before-side-effect-that-spawns-a-racing-terminator` (that row is the ORDERING of one path's own CAS-vs-side-effect for a lost notification; this row is a SECOND thread's terminal CAS invalidating a free path's quiescence assumption). Reproduces only under load/IOCP/coverage timing; prove with the harshest-condition pass (N×100 `--retries 0`) plus a teeth test that races a concurrent free against the owner's settle (trap fires in the CAS→marker gap; the free must wait on the flag) and FAILS under ASan with a heap-use-after-free when the claim is moved after the CAS. | fix/v060-supervisor-restart-wake (#58/#2), `ac39f51f`: after the terminal-CAS-before-mailbox-close reorder, an external `hew_actor_trap` CAS-ed a still-dispatching child `Running → Crashed`; `actor_free_state_is_quiescent` (`hew-runtime/src/actor.rs`) treated `Crashed` as quiescent, so the async supervisor-driven `hew_actor_free` reclaimed the box+mailbox while the owning worker was still in its `activate_actor` settle — UAF surfacing as a corrupted msg-node tripping the envelope-mode P5.2 guard on Windows-IOCP in `child_supervisor_recovery_recreates_nested_subtree` (copy-mode-only test, so no real envelope node could exist). Fixed with `HewActor::dispatch_active` (native + WASM mirror at the same C-ABI offset; layout assert updated) set by an `ActivationOwnership` RAII guard at the `Runnable → Running` CAS and cleared on every `activate_actor` exit; `hew_actor_free_inner`'s quiescence wait now requires `!dispatch_active`. Regression test `activation_owns_actor_across_external_trap_until_settle` (scheduler.rs) fails when the guard is neutered; 100/100 `--retries 0`. The gate's prescribed cross-thread mailbox-drain in the trap was rejected on the single-consumer grounds above. STRENGTHENED by fix/v060-activation-cas-gap (`0eb7ba18`): the initial fix set `dispatch_active` just AFTER the `Runnable → Running` CAS, leaving a CAS→marker gap where the actor was `Running` with the flag still `false`; a trap landing there (`Running → Crashed`) plus the async free observing `Crashed && !dispatch_active` reclaimed the box under the still-running worker — the same UAF in a narrower window. Fixed by claiming the flag BEFORE the CAS and clearing it on the lost-CAS early return (safe-from-clobber because an actor dispatches on at most one worker per epoch). New tests: `activation_claims_ownership_before_running_cas_closes_gap` (races a concurrent `hew_actor_free` against the settle — trips an ASan heap-use-after-free on the flag store when the claim is moved back after the CAS) and `lost_running_cas_clears_optimistic_dispatch_active`; 100/100 recovery + clean ASan/LSan on the lib gate. |

### `ownership-over-locks` — fix lifetimes first, then add the smallest lock surface that remains

- **area**: runtime, concurrency, networking
- **invariant**: Shared-mutable-state correctness comes from clean ownership and causality, not from layered locks. When a protocol writer shares a stream, the lock surface must match the protocol's atomic unit (full frame), not the syscall.
- **why**: A broken lifetime model cannot be rescued by mutexes — at best the locks paper over the next mile of races. Mismatched lock granularity (syscall vs. protocol) admits interleaved bytes mid-frame, which is undebuggable from logs.

| id | trigger | apply | evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ownership-over-locks` | Shared mutable state crosses threads, actors, or background workers. | Prefer `Arc`, atomics, owned routing tables, and mailbox-carried context, never pass stack pointers across threads, then add the smallest lock surface still required. | PR #784. |
| `split-framer-write-atomicity` | Multiple protocol framers or writers can write to the same socket, fd, or stream. | Identify every write-capable framer over a shared stream, acquire one per-connection operation gate around complete send/read-auto-flush/control-frame operations before any stream write, document lock ordering, and add deterministic short-write coverage that attempts a competing writer. If a close/drop path skips the gate, first remove sibling writers and document that invariant. | PR #1637 (closed #1632). |
| `held-lock-invokes-callback` | A closure is invoked while a global lock (or any non-trivially-scoped lock) is held. | Prefer "extract data under lock, run callback outside" — read what you need, release the lock, then invoke the user closure with the extracted snapshot. Holding the lock across closure invocation invites nested-lock deadlock if the callback re-enters any mutex that another path holds while trying to take this one. The same pattern that `hew-runtime/src/shutdown.rs:401-405` already implements (`std::mem::take` then iterate without lock) is the canonical shape. | A14 memory-safety audit 2026-05-24. Sites: `hew-runtime/src/lifetime/live_actors.rs` `with_live_actor`/`with_live_actor_by_id` invoke `f` while holding the global `LIVE_ACTORS` lock — latent nested-lock deadlock if `f` re-enters an actor mutex another path holds while taking `LIVE_ACTORS`. Canonical safe shape: `hew-runtime/src/shutdown.rs` (`std::mem::take` then iterate without the lock). |
| `bg-thread-mailbox-delivery-toctou` | A background thread (reactor/poller/timer) delivers into an actor mailbox or dereferences an actor pointer it holds across a poll cycle, while that actor can be freed concurrently by teardown. | A by-value liveness check *before* the send is a TOCTOU window — the actor can free between the check and the send. Synchronize detach with delivery via **publish-then-revalidate + an in-flight guard**: the delivering thread publishes the target into a `SeqCst` slot, re-validates the registration is still present *after* publishing (abort if detach already removed it), and the detach path performs the registry eviction synchronously under lock THEN spin-waits on the published guard before returning (so the free cannot proceed while a delivery is in flight). Both guard accesses `SeqCst`; registry accesses lock-ordered; clear the guard on every delivery exit (early-abort and post-delivery). The single-slot guard is sound only if the reactor processes ready fds sequentially. **The detach MUST scrub the actor from EVERY table its registration can occupy, not just the live one.** A registration that lives in a two-stage pipeline — queued in a `pending` add-list, then *promoted* into the live registry by the bg thread on its next drain — is invisible to a teardown that scans only the live registry: the actor frees while still queued, the bg thread promotes the dangling registration with no liveness re-check, and the next readiness event delivers to freed memory. Scrub the actor's `pending` add entries (keyed by stable actor identity) in the same locked detach phase that scrubs the live registry, AND extend the in-flight guard to cover the *promotion* hand-off (publish a promotion guard in the same locked section that pops the add from `pending`, spin-wait on it in detach). Pop the pending queue one entry at a time under the lock so the guard publication and the queue removal are atomic — a bulk `mem::take` re-opens the window. **The re-scrub-after-wait must itself be scrub-then-wait, LOOPED to quiescence — never a one-shot wait-then-rescrub.** A teardown that waits the guard once, re-scrubs the registry, then returns leaves a residual UAF: the bg thread can finish the promotion (clear the guard) and begin a delivery for the freshly-promoted fd in the *same poll cycle* — publishing the delivery guard *after* the wait exits but before the re-scrub — so the detach removes the registration and returns while a send is in flight. The scrub must be ordered BEFORE the wait (so any delivery the bg thread begins afterward re-validates under the lock, finds the registration gone, and aborts), and the loop repeats `wait → re-scrub → re-check` until a scrub observes the key absent from BOTH `pending` and the registry with NEITHER guard set. Termination holds because detach runs synchronously from teardown while the actor is quiescent: no new pending add for the key can appear, so the bg thread can promote only a bounded, shrinking set, and once the last is drained+scrubbed its re-validate fails and it starts no further delivery. **When the readiness edge's whole action is a single atomic state CAS (e.g. a wake that re-enqueues a `Suspended` actor), the publish-then-revalidate guard collapses to a simpler shape: perform the liveness check AND the CAS INSIDE the registry-lock critical section (`with_live_actor`, which holds the `LIVE_ACTORS` lock across its closure) so the check-and-act is atomic — every free path `untrack`s the actor under that same lock before reclaiming the box, so while the closure runs the box cannot be freed, and a stale pointer is dropped not dereferenced.** Only a lock-FREE follow-up that does not touch the actor (push onto the global run-queue) may run after the lock drops, and only because the successful `Suspended → Runnable` CAS already latched the actor out of any racing free (the free path waits for a quiescent state and CASes `Idle → Stopped`; `Runnable` is non-quiescent). Do NOT dereference a raw actor pointer carried on a channel/registration across a teardown edge without this check — nothing nulls such a back-pointer when the referent is freed, and shutdown frees actors in nondeterministic `HashMap` order. **The post-publish liveness RE-validation must ALSO be non-dereferencing for a local actor.** Publishing the `SeqCst` guard does not by itself protect the deref: a detach that runs ENTIRELY inside the snapshot→publish window sees the guard still 0, does not spin-wait, and frees the actor before the delivering thread reaches the check — so a raw `actor_ref_is_alive`-style probe that loads `(*actor).actor_state` is a UAF even though the guard is "in place". Route the local-actor liveness through the same `with_live_actor` membership-under-lock discipline as the CAS wake (a freed actor is reported dead by absence, never dereferenced); reserve the by-value-snapshot probe for REMOTE refs, which carry no actor pointer to deref. **When the readiness edge carries a SEPARATE refcounted object (a read slot, reply channel, or any heap value the delivery deposits into), and the deposit runs lock-FREE after the snapshot, the in-flight guard does NOT protect that object — it gates the ACTOR free, not the sibling's free.** The registration-owned ref + a `Drop for Registration` single-authority release is insufficient: the detach's Phase-1 scrub drops the `Registration` (and its object ref) BEFORE the Phase-2 guard wait, and teardown that destroyed the coroutine first already dropped the creator ref, so the scrub can drop the object's LAST ref and free it while the deposit is mid-flight. The delivering thread must take its OWN independent in-flight ref on the object UNDER the registry lock (in the same locked snapshot that copies the pointer, where the registration's ref proves the object live), and release that in-flight ref on EVERY exit (an RAII guard is the robust shape) — keeping `Drop for Registration` as the authority for the registration-owned ref only. Separately, when attaching a background delivery source to an actor, refuse fail-closed any mailbox policy whose eviction frees a queued node's payload without running the consuming handler (bounded `DropOld`/`Coalesce`) unless the payload carries drop-glue — naive evict-time drop-glue double-frees the handler-consumed happy path. | Reactor delivering socket reads into actor mailboxes, 2026-06-02→06-06. Dekker `DELIVERING_ACTOR` guard + synchronous detach closes the dead-actor-while-registered window (`d7f0d285`; precedent `timer_periodic`). Successive cross-ecosystem reviews peeled each shape: the `Pending::Add` promotion path needed its own `PROMOTING_ACTOR` guard + pending scrub (`9fd1f045`); the one-shot wait-then-rescrub left a residual UAF, fixed by looping phase 2 as scrub-then-wait to quiescence (`7277b66e`); non-blocking `await` made `enqueue_resume` deref a raw freed `caller_actor` back-pointer → routed through the in-`with_live_actor` check-and-CAS (`ef9cf59d`); the resume-mode read-slot snapshot copied a raw pointer with no in-flight retain so the lock-free deposit raced the Phase-1 scrub — `Drop for Registration` as "single authority" WAS the bug, fixed with an independent under-lock in-flight ref + `InflightSlotRef` RAII guard (`6d7d1db9`/`ac01b80a`); read-slot lifecycle symbols moved `stable`→`codegen-stable` (`419c86e7`). Each UAF reproduced under ASan/`MallocScribble` and pinned by a forced-ordering deterministic regression. |
| `lock-protected-lookup-copy-under-lock` | A registry/cache accessor returns `&'static str`/`&T` into a lock-protected allocation and a caller calls `.to_owned()`/`format!`/any retaining copy on the result AFTER the accessor returns (i.e. after the guard has dropped). | A lock-protected lookup that returns a borrow into the protected allocation must perform any retaining copy INSIDE the lock's critical section. Copying after the accessor returns is a lookup-to-copy TOCTOU use-after-free: a concurrent path that frees the backing allocation under the same mutex can acquire the lock in the window between the accessor returning (lock released) and the caller finishing its copy (still reading the freed bytes). "Copies immediately at the call site" is NOT safe — the question is whether the copy is inside the lock's critical section. Route retaining copies through an owned-lookup helper that copies as the tail expression of the accessor closure (so the copy executes while the guard is still live); audit every `lookup_*_by_ptr`-style accessor that returns a borrow for borrow-escape-across-clear; make the `&T` → owned `T` conversion the closure's return type, not the caller's first statement. The `PoisonSafe::access` (and equivalent `Mutex::lock`+closure patterns) shape means the closure return VALUE is computed under the guard but any operation the CALLER performs on that value is post-release — only the tail expression of the closure is inside the critical section. | PR #2107 — `lookup_dispatch_type_owned` copy-under-lock fix; `DISPATCH_TYPE_REGISTRY.access` releases the guard on closure-return so the prior `lookup_dispatch_type(..).to_owned()` call-site copy was post-release. The cross-ecosystem GPT review caught the race two same-ecosystem security passes missed. |

### `monotonic-epoch-single-clock` — a windowed comparison must use the same monotonic epoch that recorded the timestamps

- **area**: runtime, supervisor, circuit breaker, any windowed/recency/duration comparison over monotonic timestamps
- **invariant**: A "is this timestamp within the window?" comparison must derive `now` from the SAME monotonic epoch that produced the timestamps being compared. Two independently-initialized `OnceLock<Instant>` (or equivalent) epochs captured at different moments silently skew under load: a freshly-recorded timestamp may read as "in the future" of a second epoch, causing the window guard to drop it. The structural enforcement is ONE process-wide epoch: a single lazily-initialized `OnceLock<Instant>` that every "duration/timestamp since process start" reads through (`crate::monotonic` in `hew-runtime`), so there is no second epoch to skew against and cross-subsystem timestamps (crash, tracing, supervisor, timers, SWIM) share one zero point by construction. A per-subsystem `static EPOCH` is a latent instance of this defect even before any two are compared — it makes that subsystem's clock independently rebasable. A genuinely instance-local epoch (e.g. a metrics ring whose timestamps are dashboard-relative and never compared cross-subsystem) is the only sanctioned exception, and must be annotated as deliberately local.
- **why**: Fail-OPEN defect — a silently-dropped timestamp makes a windowed count come up short, so a circuit breaker stays closed, a rate-limiter under-counts, or a recency gate passes stale data. Timing-dependent: the skew is usually sub-millisecond (false-green), but under load or coverage instrumentation the two epochs diverge enough to reproduce. Threading `now_ns` from the recording site fixes ONE comparison; collapsing all process epochs to one accessor removes the entire class — a new comparison added later cannot reintroduce the skew because there is only one clock to read.

| id | trigger | apply | evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `monotonic-epoch-single-clock` | A windowed/recency/duration comparison reads `now` from a different monotonic epoch than the one that recorded the timestamps; OR a helper that compares timestamps takes no `now` param and derives its own `Instant::now()`; OR a subsystem declares its OWN `static EPOCH: OnceLock<Instant>` / `get_or_init(Instant::now)` for "duration since process start" instead of reading the shared process epoch — including in a SIBLING CRATE (`hew-std` and friends), where a private epoch is the same defect at one more remove, not a separate concern. | Read every "duration/timestamp since process start" through the ONE process-wide epoch accessor (`hew_runtime::monotonic::{process_epoch, monotonic_ns, monotonic_ms}`, re-exported as `crate::monotonic` inside `hew-runtime`) — never declare a new per-module `static EPOCH`. A crate that already depends on `hew-runtime` (e.g. `hew-std`) reads through the exported `hew_runtime::monotonic`; the dependency edge is the home, so a new clock crate is unwarranted (the cycle that would force one does not exist — `hew-runtime` does not depend on `hew-std`). Pass `now_ns` from the recording site through to the comparison function as a parameter when a single function both records and compares; never re-derive `now` from a second module-level epoch inside the comparison helper. Audit all monotonic epoch sources workspace-wide, not just in `hew-runtime` (`grep -rn "EPOCH\|get_or_init(Instant::now)" hew-runtime/src hew-std/src`): any `static EPOCH` outside the shared module is the smell. The ONLY sanctioned exception is a self-contained instance-local axis (e.g. a metrics-ring `epoch` field whose timestamps are dashboard-relative and never compared cross-subsystem); annotate it as deliberately local. | PR #2039 / a05b6aa0 — circuit breaker failed to open under load (4/200 runs) because `hew_crash_stats_recent_count` used its own `crash.rs` epoch while `circuit_breaker_record_crash` recorded timestamps against the `supervisor.rs` epoch; the skew caused freshly-recorded crashes to read as "future" and be silently dropped; point-fixed by threading `now_ns` from the recording call site into the count function. Root cause removed in 4d84052b (CAP-09): six independent process-clock epochs (`io_time::monotonic_ms`, `swim_driver::real_now_ms` — which falsely claimed to reuse io_time's epoch, `lib.rs` wasm `hew_now_ms`, `tracing::monotonic_ns`, `crash::monotonic_time_ns`, `supervisor::monotonic_time_ns`) collapsed into one `crate::monotonic` `OnceLock<Instant>`; crash's never-zero `+1` and tracing's ns precision preserved at the call sites. The seventh — `hew-std`'s `hew_datetime_now_nanos` private `static EPOCH` (issue #2060) — was folded into the same epoch via the exported `hew_runtime::monotonic::monotonic_ns`, with `now_nanos_shares_the_runtime_process_epoch` (`hew-std/src/time/datetime.rs`) priming the shared epoch, sleeping, and asserting the datetime reading reflects the slept gap (it reads ~0 from a fresh zero point on the unfolded body). The `profiler::metrics::MetricsRing.epoch` was left as the sanctioned instance-local exception (ring-relative dashboard axis, never cross-compared). |

## P1 — Parity, tests, diagnostics, and toolchain trust

### `parity-or-tracked-gap` — every user-facing surface ships in matching shape on every target, or names the gap

- **area**: native/wasm runtime, specs, stdlib surface, REPL/CLI/eval
- **invariant**: User-facing behaviour must match across native and WASM targets, and across CLI/REPL/eval entry points. Spec text and `pub fn` signatures must describe the shipped surface, not aspirational or ABI-typed names. Where parity cannot land yet, it must be a named tracked gap.
- **why**: Surface drift is the cheapest way to ship two compilers under one name. Users who learn the spec, then hit the runtime, then hit the second target should see the same shape every time.

| id | trigger | apply | evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `native-wasm-parity` | A runtime, scheduler, timer, channel, or actor behavior changes. | Implement both lanes or add a named TODO, add contract tests for timeout, cancel, and budget edges, and document intentional divergence where parity cannot land yet. For session-lifecycle hooks: `session_reset` must be called from both `hew_sched_shutdown` paths (`scheduler_wasm.rs` and `scheduler.rs`) so cleanup fires symmetrically. `task_scope` is absent on WASM today (`WASM-TODO(#1451)` at `task_scope.rs:782-783`); runtime cleanup paths that rely on scope cancel or structured concurrency must explicitly account for this gap — actor terminate callbacks are the only WASM-safe teardown path until #1451 closes. New admitted constructs in the sandbox compiler (`hew-sandbox-wasm`) MUST add a `REQUIRED_PARITY_TEST_NAMES` entry in the SAME commit (`hew-sandbox-wasm/src/lib.rs`), with a compiled-and-run parity case under `HEW_SEED=42` asserting matching stdout and exit code; alternatively, pin as explicitly unsupported with a diagnostic in `tests/unsupported-gates.test.mjs`. Security-sensitive native rejections (e.g. `PlatformLimitation` for `crypto.random_bytes` on wasm32) MUST carry explicit parity coverage — a silent sandbox compilation success where native rejects is a security gap, not a NYI gap. | PR #818/#787/#785/#754/#729; PR #1271; grounding doc 2026-05-08 async-cancel×closable investigation. | `one-construct-one-lowering-shell` | A language construct (generator/`gen`, closure, machine, `await`, **a generic call**) appears in two or more syntactic positions (standalone fn vs actor `receive` handler vs block expression; **a bare-identifier callee vs a module-qualified `module.fn(...)` callee**) and each position has its own HIR/MIR lowering arm OR its own type-checker body-setup arm. | Both positions MUST route the body through the SAME shell — at lowering (push the same enclosing context onto the same stack, wrap in the same IR node; **seed the same monomorphisation side-tables**) AND in the type checker (shape `current_return_type` / `in_generator` identically before checking the body), or the position that forgot a step diverges at that layer while the other works. A direct call to a generic free fn is one such construct: a bare callee parses as `Expr::Call`→`lower_regular_call`→`record_monomorphisation`, but a `module.fn(...)` callee parses as `Expr::MethodCall`→`lower_method_call`'s `RewriteModuleQualifiedToFunction` arm — a DIFFERENT arm that must perform the SAME per-instantiation seeding (insert the `MonoKey`, seed `call_site_type_args[site]`) or the qualified-callee position falls through to the MIR "function call" `E_NOT_YET_IMPLEMENTED` while the bare position works. Extract the shared registration tail into ONE helper both arms call (no third special-case), and make `MonoKey.origin_name` equal the emitted `BindingRef.name` so the registry `mangled_name` and the MIR re-mangling spine agree. A `gen fn` and a `receive gen fn` are the same construct: `lower_generator_fn_body` pushed the declared Yield type onto `generator_yield_tys` and wrapped the body in `HirExprKind::GenBlock`; the actor path (`lower_actor_receive_fn`) did neither, so every `yield` in a `receive gen fn` hit an empty stack ("yield expression has no enclosing generator yield type") and MIR bailed with an UnsupportedNode "separate lane" diagnostic. Mirror the shared shell (new `lower_actor_generator_body`), then lower the handler as a generator (`is_generator: true`, generator-typed MIR return) so it routes through the existing `GenBlock`→`Terminator::Yield` state machine — the handler becomes a `MakeGenerator` shell + sibling `__hew_gen_body_*`. The SAME asymmetry recurred in the type checker and failed OPEN: `check_fn_decl` stores `current_return_type = Generator<Yield, Unit>` (registration wraps a standalone gen fn as `Ty::generator(declared, Unit)`), so `Stmt::Return` extracts the Unit Return component and rejects `return <T>;`; but `check_actor_receive_fn` registered the handler as `Ty::stream(declared)` and stored the bare yield type, so `as_generator()` returned `None`, `return <T>;` was checked against the bare yield type and SILENTLY ACCEPTED (value dropped) while a valid bare `return;` was wrongly rejected. Fix: shape `current_return_type` as `Ty::generator(yield_ty, Unit)` in the actor path too, so `Stmt::Return` (Unit) and `synthesize_yield` (Yield) both extract from the same generator shape as standalone. When a construct fails OPEN at typecheck (accepts a dropped value), it is more dangerous than a fail-closed lowering gap — the body emits and miscompiles silently. Where the second position's full semantics can't land yet (here: the consumer-side `actor.gen()`→per-call channel-backed `Stream<T>` dispatch bridge, and generator bodies that read actor state), keep it a NAMED fail-closed gap (NotYetImplemented at the call site, handler stays out of the message-dispatch layout), never a silent miscompile. Prove the producer survives real codegen with `hew build --emit-obj`, not just `hew check` (codegen-front). | actor `receive gen fn` yield lowering + return-type enforcement (v0.5.3): mirrors the root↔imported asymmetry in `imported-impl-method-lowering-parity`. Cross-module generic free-fn direct call (v0.6): the `RewriteModuleQualifiedToFunction` arm registered no monomorphisation, so `module.first([1,2,3])` hit the MIR "function call" NYI while a bare `first([1,2,3])` worked; fixed by extracting `register_free_fn_monomorphisation` and calling it from both arms. |
| `cross-layer-name-gate-agreement` | A checker AND a downstream IR pre-pass (HIR/MIR) both gate on a method or identifier NAME — a reserved-name special-case like `.send` — where the correct behaviour depends on a CONTEXT discriminator (e.g. `await`-position → ask vs bare-call → tell). | A name-keyed gate duplicated across IR layers must agree on the CONTEXT discriminator, not just the name. Fixing one layer while the other keeps the name-only gate leaves a half-fixed feature: the fixed layer now routes correctly but the unfixed layer re-applies the gate by name alone, breaking the context-sensitive case. The layers must agree on both the name AND the resolved classification.
